Commentary.Commentary: Full-time at the Rose Bowl - That wraps up the second encounter at the Rose Bowl, where England Women get the better of their neighbours, Ireland Women. But the ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026 rolls on, and the action now moves to a busy day of cricket with a triple-header lined up on Wednesday, 18th June. First up, Bangladesh Women take on Australia Women at 9.30 am GMT, before India Women face Netherlands Women at 1.30 pm GMT (7 pm IST). Both games will be played at Headingly, Leeds. In the third game of the day, South Africa Women go up against Pakistan Women at Edgbaston in Birmingham, with that contest set to begin at 5.30 pm GMT. As always, do join us early for all the build-up to all three games. Until then, cheers and goodbye!

The victorious skipper of England Women - Nat Sciver-Brunt says she is really happy to win two differently looking games but is happy to get over the line. On what pleased her the most from this game, she details that the way they bowled as a unit and restricted Ireland to a low total was impressive. She acknowledges Ireland had plans to take the game away at times, but the bowlers stayed in control on a good wicket. On her getting retired out and overall fitness, Sciver-Brunt clarifies it was purely precautionary after feeling some tightness in her calf. About the group standings, she stresses England cannot afford to take any game lightly, pointing to the last T20 World Cup, where it came down to net run rate, and adds that the focus is simply on keeping the momentum going in the same manner.

The captain of Ireland Women - On Ireland's total, Gaby Lewis says they know 118 is probably below par and ideally they want to get closer to 150. She adds that the late partnership, particularly from Louisa, gave them a bit of a boost. At the halfway stage, the score felt under par, but after the way they started with the ball, she admits another 20 runs might have made a big difference. Overall, she says she is proud of the group's effort. On areas to improve, she admits the Powerplay with the bat remains an area they need to address. Losing three wickets early is far from ideal and only makes life tougher for the middle order. On the positive side, she praises the bowling effort and says the energy in the field was outstanding. She believes that if they can carry those aspects forward, they will be in a good place. On the positives from the performance, she says there are plenty of encouraging signs. She points to the way Ireland finish strongly with the bat and highlights several impressive performances with the ball. Aimee Maguire, in particular, earns special praise for bringing great energy and a real willingness to learn. She adds that the more opportunities Maguire gets against top sides like England, the better she will become. On lessons ahead of the next match, she says the team learns more about the conditions, especially under lights, which remains a relatively new experience for some of the players. She adds that every game is an opportunity to learn and improve, and the squad is already looking forward to the next challenge against New Zealand.
Let's hear from the captains now...

The Irish show heart in defeat - Ireland Women can take plenty of positives from this bowling display. Aimee Maguire struck twice early to put England under pressure, while Orla Prendergast was the standout performer, returning excellent figures of 2/17. The support cast chipped in admirably, though some sloppy ground fielding cost them at crucial moments. In the end, they simply did not have enough runs on the board. Despite pushing England far harder than expected, Ireland slipped to their second successive defeat of the World Cup.

Ireland struggle to get going - Earlier in the game, Ireland Women could only manage a well below-par total, with Orla Prendergast's gritty 26 and a late cameo from Louise Little, who struck 26 off just 15 balls, helping them get closer to the 120-run mark. Beyond those two, the innings never really took off, with six single-digit scores underlining their batting struggles. England's bowlers were simply too good, with Sophie Ecclestone leading the charge with a three-wicket haul, Danielle Gibson picking up two, and every other bowler except Freya Kemp getting among the wickets as well.

Experienced pair seals the deal - England Women began the chase steadily, but the game suddenly came alive when both openers fell in identical fashion in the same over, leaving the hosts wobbling at 27/2, soon becoming 35/3. With the innings threatening to unravel, the experienced duo of Heather Knight and skipper Nat Sciver-Brunt took charge. Their composed 64-run partnership all but shut the door on Ireland's hopes. Knight fell before the finish line, while Sciver-Brunt retired out on 48 with some concern, leading to an untidy end to the chase. It was hardly a flawless display, but England had done enough to secure the two points.

PLAYER OF THE MATCH - Sophie Ecclestone wins the award for her amazing bowling spell of 3/22. On being asked about the win, Sophie Ecclestone says it is nice to get a couple of wins under their belt and hopes England can keep the momentum going. On entering the top five wicket-takers list, she admits she was not really aware of the milestone and says it is nice to hear, but quickly shifts focus to what matters most, contributing to the team's success, and sets her sights on making it three wins from three next time out. On her role in the side, Ecclestone says she just wants to keep taking wickets and adds that England are fortunate to have a great attack with both spin and seam options to call upon.

England get the job done - England Women make it two wins from two, but this was far from the commanding performance they would have hoped for. Chasing a modest target, many expected the hosts to cruise to victory, yet Ireland Women made them scrap for every single run. Credit to the Irish for their relentless fight and disciplined bowling, while England's innings was also littered with some puzzling shot selection. They got the job done in the end, but performances like this could prove costly later on in the tournament..

OUT! CAUGHT! Double strike from Aimee Maguire and both English openers are back in the hut now. This is flighted again, full and on off, Danni Wyatt-Hodge skips down the track, stays leg side of the ball and tries to clear the in-field on the off side but only manages to get a bit of a top edge. The ball flies towards mid off, where Gaby Lewis settles under it and takes a fine reverse cup catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Gaby Lewis b Aimee Maguire
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Aimee Maguire to Danni Wyatt-Hodge, OUT! c Gaby Lewis b Aimee Maguire.

Commentary.Commentary: Floated, full and on leg, Nat Sciver-Brunt clips it through square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Aimee Maguire to Nat Sciver-Brunt, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Ireland have their first breakthrough. But they need more. Nat Sciver-Brunt, the English skipper, walks out to bat at number 3.

OUT! TAKEN! Aimee Maguire strikes on her return to the attack. She tosses it up, full and on off, Amy Jones backs away and tries to loft it over extra cover but her bat turns in her hands. She ends up mistiming it high in the air wide of mid off, where Gaby Lewis moves to her left, keeps her eyes on the ball and takes a good catch, tumbling on the ground. England Women are 27/1, chasing 119 runs.
Commentary.Howout: c Gaby Lewis b Aimee Maguire
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Aimee Maguire to Amy Jones, OUT! c Gaby Lewis b Aimee Maguire.

Commentary.Commentary: Aimee Maguire (1-0-6-0) is back on. She replaces Arlene Kelly.
Back of a length and down the leg side, Amy Jones tries to hook it away but gloves it towards short fine for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Orla Prendergast to Amy Jones, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Much fuller and around off, Amy Jones drives it firmly but straight to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Orla Prendergast to Amy Jones, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hits the deck hard and on off, Amy Jones stabs it out to short cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Orla Prendergast to Amy Jones, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Oh, that's lovely! A half-volley and on off, Amy Jones leans onto her drive and creams it between extra cover and mid off for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Orla Prendergast to Amy Jones, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Good length and on off, Danni Wyatt-Hodge guides it away through point for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Orla Prendergast to Danni Wyatt-Hodge, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Chance! Back of a length and around middle, Amy Jones shuffles across for the scoop but gets an underedge behind. The keeper, Amy Hunter, dives to her left to grab it with her outstretched glove but it just does not stick in. A single taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Orla Prendergast to Amy Jones, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: England are off to a positive start. They need 99 runs to win from 102 balls. The only way Ireland are going to win is by taking all 10 English wickets.
Hard length and on middle, Danni Wyatt-Hodge backs away and guides it towards backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Arlene Kelly to Danni Wyatt-Hodge, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Put away! Back of a length and just outside off, Danni Wyatt-Hodge gets the chance to free his arms and crunches it through cover-point for four more runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Arlene Kelly to Danni Wyatt-Hodge, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Up and over! Pitched up and around middle, Danni Wyatt-Hodge looks to loft it down the ground but does not get it from the middle of the bat. However, she gets enough to clear mid on as the ball trickles to the fence for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Arlene Kelly to Danni Wyatt-Hodge, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller one and angling into the pads, Amy Jones clips it through square leg for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Arlene Kelly to Amy Jones, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and on middle, Amy Jones nudges it through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Arlene Kelly to Amy Jones, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Good-length delivery, on middle, shaping in, Danni Wyatt-Hodge backs away and guides it towards backward point. The fielder throws it at the keeper's end, but it is a wild one and allows a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Arlene Kelly to Danni Wyatt-Hodge, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Arlene Kelly is into the attack, and she replaces Aimee Maguire.
Just short of a length and well outside off, Amy Jones slashes at it but fails to connect. End of a probing over!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Orla Prendergast to Amy Jones, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hits the deck hard, on middle, jags back in, Danni Wyatt-Hodge stabs it out towards short cover for a single.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and on of, jags back in a bit, Danni Wyatt-Hodge stays back and dabs it down towards backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Orla Prendergast to Danni Wyatt-Hodge, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Beauty! Orla Prendergast begins with a good-length delivery, on the fifth stump line, holds its line as well. Danni Wyatt-Hodge has a poke at it but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Orla Prendergast to Danni Wyatt-Hodge, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Spin in tandem? Nope. Pace it shall be. Here's Orla Prendergast into the attack. A slip in place for Wyatt-Hodge.
More air on this one, on middle too, Danni Wyatt-Hodge advances again to make it a full toss and swipes it off the inner half of the bat towards mid-wicket for one.

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Aimee Maguire to Danni Wyatt-Hodge, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: A loopy delivery, dips in late, Danni Wyatt-Hodge gets forward and blocks it out.

Commentary.Commentary: Floated full and on middle, Danni Wyatt-Hodge looks to drive it away but gets a bottom edge onto her boots as the ball rolls back to the bowler.
